[quote=astanir;60268765][spoiler=[b]The spark[/b]]
General Kaiwai sits in his new office overlooking the streets of Astan. It has been 3 days since the coup and nobody has even attempted to overthrow him. Perfect. Too perfect. Just as this thought crossed his mind, a knock came from the door.
ENTER!
A young soldier walks in carrying various documents.
Sir, I have an intelligence report for you says the soldier as he lays the documents on Kaiwais desk.
Thank you private, dismissed.
The soldier quickly scurried away and the door is shut behind him by the entrance guards. Kaiwais eyes begin to dart around the report. He smiles. He knew that a stupid move like this would come from the loyalist sooner or later. The intelligence report details the exact location of a loyalist base, where the soldiers fled after they failed, rather miserably, to stop Kaiwais coup. After the executions, the already weak loyalist army was without coherent leader, leading them to make what Kaiwai perceived as a fatal mistake.

That night, three units of troops would be directed towards the location of the loyalist base. They would travel north via armoured vehicles through the night until they reached the specified location. Just as predicted, they came across a valley, with a river running through the middle. On the opposite side of the valley, a metal compound protruded out of the side of the hill, an old relic of the civil war during the 70s. The troops would begin setting up machine guns atop the hills, facing downwards towards the compound. These would provide cover for the troops who would descend down the side of the valley and begin the assault.

At 3:00am sharp, still under the cover of darkness, a unit would slowly make their way down the valley, keeping low in the bushes to avoid detection. This would be successful and there pile reach the entrance with no resistance. First, a series of grenades would be launched inside the entrance of the compound to take out any guards. Two, three, four explosions and silence. The coast was clear. Almost too clear. The soldiers would enter the compound to find no bodies. The grenades had killed no one, because there had been no one to kill. Confused, the troops would continue further into the compound, through winding makeshift corridors lined with metal sheeting. Two soldiers would be left to guard the entrance of the compound.

The units would continue to have no resistance as they continued their search of the compound. They would find no sign of life, only empty rooms and corridors. Just as they thought that it was all a fake, a soldier spotted movement.
Sir! I saw something, a person running!
The unit would swiftly turn around and follow the person that the soldier had seen, firing their rifles. The chase would continue down several paths, until they came to a dead end, the person had disappeared. Suddenly, a soldier drops dead, blood splattering from their head. A group of armed men in uniform not that dissimilar from the attacking forces would begin shooting from round the corner. The unit had got themselves trapped.

Back outside, the two entrance guards would be no problem for the loyalists. They would swiftly stab them both in the back with standard hand knives, neutralising them instantly. Atop the hills on the other side of the valley, the machine gunners would be quick to open fire as soon as they caught sight of the situation below, but the loyalists would be protected by their compound. Additionally, several Guerilla fighters would make themselves known, assaulting the soldiers on the hills from the bushes behind. Kaiwais forces had been outplayed.

Back in Astan, Kaiwai would be notified of the situation quickly. Outraged, he would order the retreat of the units, but it would be too late. Inside the compound, the trapped unit would be quickly massacred, being unable to move backwards nor forwards. The unit on the hills would put up more of a fight, but would still be unable to escape. Surrounded by bushes filled with Guerillas and trapped in the valley, they had nowhere to run either and would eventually be picked off one by one.

Whilst the battle unfolded in the north, Astan would not be free from violence either. In response to the coup, protesters and defected soldiers would band together to march through the city streets advocating for Democracy and peace. The group began in the Western suburbs and worked towards the parliament building, but would not get far before they encountered resistance. Kaiwai would order the immediate deployment of troops into the city, where they would begin shooting on the protesters. Some would simply be scattered, but others, mainly the defected soldiers, would pull out their own weapons and begin fighting back. The clash would turn into an all out urban battle within just an hour, with Kaiwais army and the Democratic protesters taking positions opposite each other, turning the city square into no mans land. Despite the heavy resistance, the shear number of Kaiwais troops would be enough to push the protesters back and out of the city. By midday, the city would fall back under total control of Kaiwais army, with the borders now heavily reinforced.

The second Astaniran civil war has begun
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Factions arise[/b]]
Over the course of the next month, the situation in Astanir would rapidly escalate. New factions would begin fighting left, right and centre to take control over as much of the fractured country as possible. The following major factions would arise on top, as the major players of this war.

Astaniran National Forces - General Kaiwais army, which are currently in control of the government. They follow an extreme isolationist ideology, deeming any foreign influence a threat. Began fighting after the unsuccessful attempt to raid the loyalist compound and swiftly captured most of the islands southern territory.

Armed restoration front - The loyalist forces fighting to bring the old junta regime back to power. They claim to be the legitimate government of Astanir and call upon the IA to recognise them as so. Began fighting after Kaiwais forces raided their compound. They would soon establish their area of control in the north.

Democratic Army of Astanir - A coalition of pro-democracy fighters and protesters, aiming to bring an end to totalitarianism in Astanir and transition towards a democratic state. Began fighting after the protest in Astan turned bloody. After the protest, the group would retreat eastwards and fortify their position against both Kaiwai and the loyalists.

Amaralo Peoples Army - A group of armed fighters based on Astanirs archipelagos in the Amaralo ocean, who identify themselves closer to the Amaralo continent than Argos or shamat. They advocate for either independence from the rest of Astanir, or the overthrow of the regime and the placement of a pro-Amaralo pro-pantagrueli government. They are suspected to be backed by the pantagrueli government, but nothing has been confirmed. They began fighting during an uprising on Astanirs outlying Amaralo islands against the loyalists who occupied the islands and would easily take control over most of the Amaralo islands in a coordinated attack.

Argossian Militias - Armed aboriginal Argossian tribes fighting for independence from Astanir after years of occupation and oppression from the junta government. They are currently not a collective faction, but rather tens of tribal militias fighting towards a common cause. Began fighting after Kaiwais forces destroyed various aboriginal villages during a push against the loyalists. As of now they only hold small individual settlements and protect themselves against both loyalists and Kaiwais army.
[/spoiler]
